title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Found Its Way by Settling for Less
summary: After a disastrous third season, the return of Jason Sudeikis' warmhearted Apple comedy didn't take the same big swings that helped make it a mega-hit. Instead, Season 4 acclimated to its comfy sitcom environs, becoming a little less ambitious — and a lot easier to enjoy.

title: With Trump Settlement Money in the Bank, E. Jean Carroll Finally Speaks — and in Time for the Documentary Oscar Race
summary: Exclusive: After staying mum as Donald Trump's various appeals moved through the courts, Carroll can finally talk. Read our previously embargoed interview with the subject of "Ask E. Jean" here.

title: One-Night Only Screenings of ‘Wicker’ in 4DX Will Let Horny Fans Feel Every Creak and Splinter
summary: Black Bear will host special event screenings of the steamy Sundance darling starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård on October 28.

title: Athlete-Owned Production Companies Are Everywhere — Which Ones Are Working?
summary: From LeBron James and Steph Curry to Tom Brady and Peyton Manning, it seems like every star athlete has waded into Hollywood in the past decade. A few blueprints for success are starting to emerge.

title: ‘Soul Patrol’ Trailer: A Historic Group of Black Vietnam War Veterans Reunite to Reckon with the Past
summary: Exclusive: The winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival will head to theaters starting November 6, just in time for Veterans Day.

title: ‘The Social Reckoning’ Is the Kind of Film That the Oscars Have Moved Past Recognizing
summary: Aaron Sorkin's "The Social Reckoning" is a fine film. It is just not cinematic in the way Oscar voters are looking for.

title: ‘My Undesirable Friends: Part II — Exile’ Review: Don’t Be Intimidated by Julia Loktev’s Gripping Six-Hour Wartime Journalism Epic
summary: Epic may be the wrong word for what Loktev achieves with her follow-up to the Oscar-shortlisted saga about Russian dissident journalists condemned by the Kremlin — it's really more of a vibe movie, and better for it.

title: James Gray Looks Back at His Confident, Dangerous First Film ‘Little Odessa’
summary: The writer/director of "Paper Tiger" talks to IndieWire about his 1994 debut "Little Odessa," now available in a new 4K UHD edition from Criterion.

title: ‘The Social Reckoning’ Review: Aaron Sorkin’s Facebook Files Only Expose Bad Performances and an Even Lousier Script
summary: Oscar winner Mikey Madison and Jeremy Allen White star as a whistleblower and a reporter with a dream (opposite a miscast Jeremy Strong) in a draggy, so-what journo drama that's more agitprop for the Sorkin brand than a paean to the press.

title: Why Harry Potter and Gandalf Won’t Be Teaming Up with Optimus Prime
summary: Complicated licensing agreements prevent David Ellison from pulling off crossovers between Paramount and Warner Bros.' biggest franchises, which is probably a good thing.

title: Why Is Gen Z Obsessed with the Oldest ‘American Horror Story’?
summary: Gen Z didn't inherit Ryan Murphy's horror anthology as appointment viewing, but recent Nielsen data and the TV show's most clippable fragments reveal a special connection with its beginning.

title: Eva Marie Saint, Oscar-Winning ‘On the Waterfront’ and ‘North by Northwest’ Star, Dead at 102
summary: The Hollywood icon enjoyed a stage and screen acting career that lasted eight decades.
